title: Case Study: Rescuing a Slow Dashboard
objective: After this lesson you will be able to execute the full optimization workflow on a realistic slow query — reproduce, EXPLAIN, hypothesize once, fix minimally (rewrite then index), verify with plans and timings, and document the change so the win survives.
why: Technique chapters teach moves; production demands game sense — which move first, how you know it worked, and how you prove it to reviewers. This lesson is a narrated rescue of a dashboard query exhibiting four stacked pathologies, applying Chapters 1–7 in order. Read it as the template for every future 'the dashboard is slow' ticket.

blocks.text: The learner-engagement dashboard loads in 4.2s and timeouts under load. The query: per-course totals, completion rates, top-learner names, filtered by topic search, sorted by rate, page 40 of OFFSET pagination. Four pathologies stack: leading-wildcard LIKE, correlated scalar per row, OFFSET deep page, missing composite index. One fix at a time — watch attribution work.

blocks.code:
-- The patient (real SQLite/PostgreSQL, simplified for study)
-- SELECT c.title,
--   (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM enrollments e WHERE e.course_id = c.id) AS total,
--   (SELECT name FROM developers d JOIN enrollments x ON x.developer_id = d.id
--    WHERE x.course_id = c.id ORDER BY x.progress DESC LIMIT 1) AS top_learner
-- FROM courses c
-- WHERE c.topic LIKE '%end%' AND c.published = 1
-- ORDER BY total DESC LIMIT 20 OFFSET 780;
blocks.caption: Four stacked pathologies — diagnose before touching anything

blocks.text: Never optimize a description: reproduce with EXPLAIN (QUERY PLAN) plus timing (`timer on` in SQLite CLI, EXPLAIN ANALYZE in PG) on production-shaped data. Baselines recorded: 4.2s wall time; plan shows SCAN courses (LIKE '%end%' unindexable), two correlated scalars per course row, TEMP B-TREE over the full sort before OFFSET discards 780 rows. Every number below is measured against this baseline — no baseline, no proof.

Flatten the correlated scalars into one grouped derived table (Ch.3): one enrollments pass instead of 2N. Replace the leading-wildcard search with an exact topic match plus a documented follow-up (trigram/full-text search is the real fix for substring search — scoped out, stated openly). Convert page-40 OFFSET to a keyset bookmark (Ch.3). Rewrites only: 4.2s → 1.1s. Shape beats schema.

blocks.code:
-- After rewrite: one grouped pass, sargable filter, keyset page
-- (real SQLite/PostgreSQL)
-- WITH per_course AS (
--   SELECT course_id, COUNT(*) AS total,
--     MAX(progress) AS best_progress
--   FROM enrollments GROUP BY course_id
-- )
-- SELECT c.title, COALESCE(p.total, 0) AS total
-- FROM courses c
-- LEFT JOIN per_course p ON p.course_id = c.id
-- WHERE c.topic = 'backend' AND c.published = 1
--   AND (COALESCE(p.total, 0), c.id) < (?, ?)
-- ORDER BY total DESC, c.id DESC LIMIT 20;
blocks.caption: Rewrite transcript: flatten, sargabilize, keyset — 4.2s to 1.1s

blocks.text: Re-EXPLAIN: remaining SCAN is courses filtered by topic+published (small table, acceptable) and probes into enrollments per course. One composite `ON enrollments(course_id)` converts probes to SEARCH: 1.1s → 0.18s. A covering variant shaves more, but the plain composite already beats the 0.5s budget — restraint ships (Ch.2's audit mindset: minimal effective indexing).

blocks.code:
-- The single index the plan proved necessary (real SQLite/PostgreSQL)
-- CREATE INDEX idx_enrollments_course ON enrollments(course_id);
-- Plan after: SEARCH enrollments USING INDEX per course row.
-- 1.1s → 0.18s. Total: 4.2s → 0.18s (23x), one rewrite + one index.
blocks.caption: 23x from shape first, schema second — each step measured

blocks.text: Step 4 — document so the win survives

Unoptimized queries regrow: someone re-adds OFFSET 'temporarily', a new OR defeats the index. The deliverable is a note with baseline, each change, each measurement, and the guardrails (keyset pagination contract, the documented trigram follow-up for substring search). Performance without documentation is a anecdote; with it, a maintained guarantee.

blocks.query: SELECT c.topic, COUNT(e.id) AS n FROM courses c LEFT JOIN enrollments e ON e.course_id = c.id WHERE c.published = 1 GROUP BY c.topic ORDER BY n DESC;
blocks.note: Run this dashboard-shaped flat query in the sandbox — grouped join, real filter, meaningful sort. It is the healthy end-state shape: imagine its plan (probes + small sort) versus the original's (scans + correlated scalars + deep OFFSET).

items: Reproduce + baseline first (plan + timing on production-shaped data) — no baseline, no proof
Rewrite before indexing: flatten scalars, sargabilize filters, keyset pages (4.2s → 1.1s here)
Index the plan-proven bottleneck minimally, verify SEARCH (1.1s → 0.18s here)
One change per measurement for attribution; document baselines, steps, and guardrails

exercise.prompt: Take the stalled-learners report (developers ≥1 enrollment, 0 completions, grouped by role): (a) in the sandbox, run the flat shape and record its rows; (b) write the 'slow version' deliberately (correlated scalar per developer + OFFSET page 10) and the rescued version (grouped derived table + keyset) for real SQLite/PostgreSQL; (c) write the three-line change log (baseline → rewrite → index) with what you would measure at each arrow.
hints: Sandbox flat: developers JOIN enrollments GROUP BY developer HAVING SUM(completed) = 0 — plus role via join. Record counts: the preservation target.
Slow version: SELECT with (SELECT COUNT(*) …) scalar and LIMIT 5 OFFSET 45. Rescued: derived-table aggregation LEFT JOINed, WHERE (key) bookmark, composite on the FK if the plan demands it.
Change log lines name measurement, not hope: 'EXPLAIN shows per-row scalar probes → flatten → re-EXPLAIN shows one grouped pass; wall time X → Y'.
exercise.solution:
-- (a) sandbox preservation target (flat — runs here)
-- developers with enrollments but zero completions, per role
-- (b) slow vs rescued (real SQLite/PostgreSQL):
-- SLOW: correlated scalar + OFFSET 45 (per-row probes, linear skip)
-- RESCUED: grouped derived table + LEFT JOIN + keyset bookmark
--   + CREATE INDEX iff plan shows probe SCANs.
-- (c) log: baseline plan+time → rewrite (flatten) → re-plan+time → index → verify.
exercise.why: Writing the slow version on purpose teaches pathology recognition — you cannot diagnose shapes you have never authored. The change log practices the professional deliverable: measured arrows, not adjectives.

-- Sandbox preservation target (flat — run here)
SELECT d.role, COUNT(*) AS stalled
FROM developers d
JOIN enrollments e ON e.developer_id = d.id
GROUP BY d.id, d.role
HAVING SUM(e.completed) = 0;

quiz.q: First step on a 'dashboard is slow' ticket?
options: Reproduce with EXPLAIN + timing on production-shaped data and record the baseline
quiz.explain: No baseline, no proof: every later claim (and every attribution) references the starting plan and time. Optimizing descriptions is superstition.

quiz.q: Why rewrite before indexing in the case study order?
options: Shape fixes (flatten, sargabilize, keyset) are zero-schema-cost and often larger (4.2s→1.1s); indexes then serve the proven bottleneck minimally
quiz.explain: Rewrite attacks the dominant cost with no schema commitment; indexing then serves the remaining proven need. Reversed order risks indexing a shape you later discard.

quiz.q: After flattening, the plan still shows probe SCANs into enrollments. Next move?
options: CREATE INDEX on the probe key (course_id), re-EXPLAIN, confirm SEARCH — the plan-proven minimal schema change
quiz.explain: Probes-per-row at scale dominate: one composite converts them to SEARCH. Minimal, plan-demanded, verified — the restraint half of the discipline.

quiz.q: Why document baselines, steps, and guardrails after the fix?
options: Unoptimized shapes regrow (casual OFFSETs, new ORs) — the note preserves the win as a maintained guarantee with contracts
quiz.explain: Performance rots without contracts: the keyset rule and the trigram follow-up stop well-meaning regressions. Measured history beats tribal memory.

summary: Rescue = reproduce + baseline, rewrite (flatten/sargabilize/keyset), index the proven need, verify each arrow, document the win. Shape first, schema second, proof always.
